result.summary: This PR consolidates the logic in InvalidChainFound, moving most of it into InvalidBlockFound so that ActivateBestChain and InvalidateBlock no longer duplicate logging and block-index loops. It renames InvalidChainFound to UpdateBestInvalid to reflect its narrowed responsibility, and adds a functional test for invalidateblock on out-of-chain blocks. During review, a real gap was found (missing SetBlockFailureFlags/RecalculateBestHeader calls for out-of-chain invalidation) and fixed in a later push.
result.problem: Invalid-block handling logic was duplicated across three call sites, causing duplicate log lines and duplicate O(n) loops over the block index, and making the code hard to reason about (as stratospher's summary gist documents). This addresses concerns raised in earlier PRs #31405 and #31533 about repeated work in InvalidateBlock and ActivateBestChain.

open_concerns: Crypt-iQ notes m_best_invalid may still not be set to the true best invalid block in some in-chain cases, a pre-existing issue the author says is out of scope but could be improved in a follow-up.
Crypt-iQ raised confusion about InvalidateBlock's behavior under concurrent block addition from another thread; unresolved but not treated as blocking (crACK already given).
frankomosh observed the invalidateblock log line format and prefix changed (from InvalidChainFound: to Invalidated block:), which the author addressed by explaining logs aren't a stable interface.
resolved_concerns: Missing SetBlockFailureFlags/RecalculateBestHeader calls for out-of-chain invalidateblock case, found by Crypt-iQ, fixed by author with an added regression test.
stratospher's suggestion to merge the two block-index loops into one was declined by the author with rationale (invalidateblock is a rare/costly-to-trigger path), no pushback.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Directly changes InvalidBlockFound/InvalidChainFound/InvalidateBlock logic in validation.cpp, which governs chainstate handling of invalid blocks; carries the Validation label.
categories.rationale: During review a real correctness gap was found and fixed: InvalidateBlock on an out-of-chain block was missing SetBlockFailureFlags and RecalculateBestHeader calls, which could leave block-index state inconsistent (Crypt-iQ's analysis, confirmed and fixed by the author with a regression test). The change also removes duplicate O(n) block-index loops and duplicate log lines. It is scoped to a rarely-triggered path (RPC invalidateblock, or attacker-costly invalid-PoW blocks) so impact is narrow, and a known remaining imperfection (m_best_invalid correctness) is explicitly deferred to a follow-up.

result.card: This PR refactors Bitcoin Core's invalid-block handling (InvalidChainFound/InvalidBlockFound/InvalidateBlock) to remove duplicate logging and duplicate O(n) loops over the block index, and renames InvalidChainFound to UpdateBestInvalid. During review, Crypt-iQ found a real gap: the refactor initially dropped necessary SetBlockFailureFlags/RecalculateBestHeader calls for invalidateblock on out-of-chain blocks, which the author fixed with an added regression test. The PR has a crACK from Crypt-iQ and concept ACKs from stratospher and frankomosh, with one acknowledged but deferred imperfection (m_best_invalid not always reflecting the true best invalid block) left for a follow-up. It touches only validation.cpp's invalid-block bookkeeping, not mempool policy or consensus rules, and the affected paths are rare (RPC-triggered or requiring costly invalid-PoW blocks). The PR is stale on activity (author silent 28 days) but not blocked; the code is currently reviewable.
